items.title: Derek Brown interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, March 5, 2021
items.q: like if you just look at Coltrane. You start with “Blue Trane” but then you move on.

ctx.x: Yeah well I mean I had like a kind of musical mid-life crisis in grad school, that period where I was working really hard but kind of burning out at the same time. And it came from, I specifically remember the moment. I was second year grad school — I was a grad assistant so I was supposed to be one of the top people. I was getting paid to be in school. I was in charge of a quote unquote beginning jazz combo with some freshman in it. And in came this punk saxophone kid who played circles around me. He was twice…

unique sound, it was just truly seeking what I like. And that’s another thing with that whole honestly listening to yourself. I think more musicians, or a lot of musicians, need to be honest about what they truly like in music. It’s kind of like when I was a teacher and I was teaching some of these saxophone majors, they were majors in music. They wanted to perform for a living. And like let’s say it was a classical student. And I’d say, hey have you listened to this piece? What recordings do you like? And they…

Well you just said, that was very informative and you said a word that I was going to get to. Do you think you’re obsessed with your music career? Because I know how my mind thinks. If I’m working on an arrangement or something, and I take the dog for a walk, I’m like working on this thing in my head and I forget what I’m outside to do. Like I’m just standing in the sidewalk and the dog’s looking at me like yeah? And I wonder if you are constantly trying to think what’s next for me?
